title: Namespace Shield Relay Gateway for Dedicated and On‑Prem Observability
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a relay gateway that provides per-namespace isolation and lightweight policy enforcement for Dedicated and on‑prem observability ingest. The gateway (Namespace Shield) sits at the VPC/on‑prem perimeter and normalizes telemetry envelopes (traces, metrics, logs), rewrites opaque tenant tokens to internal namespace IDs, applies soft quotas/backpressure windows, and performs host-level scrubbing and sampling hints before forwarding to our internal collectors. This reduces cross-namespace tail latency spikes, prevents noisy-neighbor ingestion storms, and enables safe replay/backfill for on‑prem installs.
goals: Provide deterministic per-namespace traffic shaping (burst tokens + sliding window) at the perimeter
Normalize envelope headers to a canonical namespace ID and attach provenance metadata for later auditability
Expose trace sampling hooks so the runtime can request trace payloads retained for quality regressions
Support a configurable scrubbing policy to strip PII from logs at the relay when requested by customer policies
Integrate with console dashboards to surface per-namespace ingest latency/error heatmaps and quota burn rate
acceptance_criteria: Gateway deployed behind VPC ingress and on‑prem edge proxy in staging and passes chaos latency tests
Per-namespace burst window enforcement demonstrated under synthetic storms (no cross-namespace amplification)
Canonical namespace header is present on all forwarded envelopes and accepted by downstream collectors
Configurable scrub policy applied and covered by automated unit/integration tests
Observed reduction in median 95th percentile ingest latency in staging by >= 30% under mixed workloads
Dashboard panel added: 'Namespace Ingest Latency & Errors' with per-namespace filters and alerting rule
notes: 2026-02-14: Kickoff — scoped initial MVP to traces + logs; metrics will be second wave. Decision: use an append-only namespace mapping service instead of in‑gateway DB to keep gateway stateless.
2026-02-20: Design review with PM/SEC — agreed on header rewrite strategy: accept customer token, validate via short-lived token introspection, replace with internal ns-id before forwarding.
2026-02-28: Prototype built for envelope normalizer (golang). POC repo: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-relay-shield PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-relay-shield/pull/12
2026-03-03: Load test 1 — gateway handled 5k rps steady-state, tail latency increased under burst; added per-namespace ring-bucket to smooth bursts.
2026-03-06: Security review requested — submitted Confluence doc with threat model and scrub policy: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Namespace+Shield+Threat+Model
2026-03-08: Feedback from infra — prefer upstream TLS termination at perimeter while gateway performs mTLS to collectors; change logged and scheduled
2026-03-10: Ran staging chaos (network partitions) — gateway correctly soft-queued envelopes with exponential backoff; two bugs found in header propagation fixed in PR #18
current_blockers: Waiting on short-lived token introspection endpoint (SEC team) and on-prem packaging approval for air-gapped tarball
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): envelope normalization, namespace mapping, per-namespace burst window, basic scrub rules
Phase 2: trace sampling hooks + trace-kept-cursor for on-demand retention, console integration for quota controls
Phase 3: metrics normalization, adaptive retention, and cluster-aware relay mesh for HA
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Gateway becomes hot-spot under extreme telemetry spikes — Mitigation: add automatic client-side throttling hints and graceful degradation to lightweight summaries
Risk: Scrubbing at perimeter may break downstream parsers — Mitigation: add schema-aware scrub rules and fingerprint tests against sample corpora
Risk: Token introspection latency adds to tail — Mitigation: cache introspection results for very short TTL and fallback to conservative namespace assignment
